topLevelSource.label: Pew Research Center, How the Global Religious Landscape Changed From 2010 to 2020 (published 2025)
topLevelSource.note: Top-level shares use Pew's 2020 global estimates. The Pew 2025 report does not subdivide the seven global categories into denominations.

christianSource.label: Pew Research Center, Global Christianity (published 2011)
christianSource.note: Christian branch proportions use Pew's 2010 global Christian estimates because the newer global landscape update does not publish equivalent denomination-level splits.

root.name: World
root.description: A map of major religious identities and the religiously unaffiliated. Population scale and taxonomy are deliberately separated.

children.name: Christianity
children.summary: The world's largest religious group in Pew's 2020 estimate. Convergence gives Christianity extra depth because it is Ryan's own tradition and because its internal branching is often hidden by one global label.

children.name: Catholic
children.summary: Pew's 2010 global Christian taxonomy placed about half of Christians in the Catholic tradition.

children.name: Latin Church
children.summary: The largest Catholic church tradition; Western liturgical and canonical tradition.

children.name: Eastern Catholic Churches
children.summary: Eastern churches in communion with Rome, including Byzantine, Alexandrian, Armenian, East Syriac, West Syriac and other traditions.

children.name: Protestant
children.summary: Pew's broad Protestant category includes Anglicans as well as independent and nondenominational churches. The family map below is orientation, not a globally proportional census.

children.name: Baptist
children.summary: Congregational Protestant traditions centered on believer's baptism and local church life.

children.name: Southern Baptist Convention
children.summary: Large U.S. Baptist convention.

children.name: National Baptist traditions
children.summary: Historically Black Baptist conventions and related bodies in the U.S.

children.name: American Baptist Churches USA
children.summary: U.S. Baptist denomination with historic Northern Baptist roots.

children.name: Independent Baptist
children.summary: Decentralized local churches and networks rather than one denomination.

children.name: Reformed Baptist
children.summary: Baptist churches shaped by Reformed theology; overlaps two family labels by design.

children.name: Reformed / Presbyterian
children.summary: Traditions shaped by Reformed theology, confessions and Presbyterian or continental church orders.

children.name: Presbyterian
children.summary: Presbyterian churches worldwide, including confessional and mainline bodies.

children.name: Continental Reformed
children.summary: Dutch, Swiss and related Reformed churches shaped by continental confessions.

children.name: Congregational / Reformed
children.summary: Historically Reformed congregational traditions.

children.name: Reformed Baptist
children.summary: A cross-tradition node: Baptist ecclesiology with Reformed theology.

children.name: Methodist / Wesleyan
children.summary: Traditions descended from the Wesleyan revival and shaped by holiness, connection and practical discipleship.

children.name: United Methodist
children.summary: Large global Methodist denomination.

children.name: Global Methodist
children.summary: Newer global Methodist body formed after recent separation from the UMC.

children.name: AME / AME Zion
children.summary: Historically Black Methodist traditions.

children.name: Wesleyan / Free Methodist
children.summary: Holiness-oriented Wesleyan denominations and networks.

children.name: Lutheran
children.summary: Churches shaped by the Lutheran confessions, with confessional and mainline/global expressions.

children.name: Confessional Lutheran
children.summary: Confessional bodies such as LCMS and analogous churches elsewhere.

children.name: Mainline / ecumenical Lutheran
children.summary: Bodies such as ELCA and many churches in the Lutheran World Federation.

children.name: Anglican
children.summary: Churches in and around the Anglican Communion, rooted in the Church of England and Prayer Book tradition.

children.name: Anglican Communion
children.summary: Global communion of autonomous Anglican provinces.

children.name: Related / continuing Anglican bodies
children.summary: Anglican bodies outside or alongside the formal Communion, including ACNA and continuing churches.

children.name: Pentecostal / Charismatic
children.summary: Spirit-focused Protestant traditions emphasizing gifts, renewal and mission.

children.name: Assemblies of God
children.summary: Large global Pentecostal fellowship.

children.name: Church of God in Christ
children.summary: Major historically Black Holiness-Pentecostal denomination.

children.name: Independent Pentecostal / Charismatic
children.summary: Large and diverse networks not captured by one denomination.

children.name: Adventist
children.summary: Protestant traditions with a strong emphasis on the Advent and, in Seventh-day Adventism, Sabbath observance.

children.name: Anabaptist
children.summary: Mennonite, Amish, Brethren and related traditions emphasizing discipleship, community and often nonviolence.

children.name: Restoration
children.summary: Restorationist Protestant movements seeking New Testament church patterns, including Churches of Christ and Christian Churches.

children.name: Independent / Nondenominational
children.summary: Independent evangelical, Bible church, seeker, network and nondenominational congregations. This category is large but hard to classify consistently across countries.

children.name: Orthodox
children.summary: Pew's 2010 global category grouped Orthodox traditions at about twelve percent of Christians.

children.name: Eastern Orthodox
children.summary: Communion of autocephalous Eastern Orthodox churches.

children.name: Greek Orthodox
children.summary: Greek-speaking and diaspora Orthodox jurisdictions.

children.name: Russian Orthodox
children.summary: Russian Orthodox Church and related tradition.

children.name: Romanian Orthodox
children.summary: Autocephalous Eastern Orthodox church centered in Romania.

children.name: Serbian Orthodox
children.summary: Autocephalous Eastern Orthodox church centered in Serbia and diaspora.

children.name: Antiochian Orthodox
children.summary: Patriarchate of Antioch and its diaspora jurisdictions.

children.name: Oriental Orthodox
children.summary: Ancient churches outside the Chalcedonian Eastern Orthodox communion.

children.name: Coptic Orthodox
children.summary: Egyptian Oriental Orthodox church.

children.name: Armenian Apostolic
children.summary: Armenian Oriental Orthodox tradition.

children.name: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo
children.summary: Large Ethiopian Oriental Orthodox church.

children.name: Syriac Orthodox
children.summary: West Syriac Oriental Orthodox tradition.

children.name: Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo
children.summary: Eritrean Oriental Orthodox church.

children.name: Malankara Orthodox
children.summary: Indian Oriental Orthodox tradition.

children.name: Other Christian
children.summary: Pew's 2010 bucket included groups that identify as Christian but are not placed in Catholic, Protestant or Orthodox categories. Classification is contested.

children.name: Latter-day Saints
children.summary: Self-identifies as Christian; many historic Christian traditions classify it outside orthodox Christianity.

children.name: Jehovah's Witnesses
children.summary: Self-identifies as Christian; many historic Christian traditions classify it outside orthodox Christianity.

children.name: Islam
children.summary: The world's second-largest religious group in Pew's 2020 estimate.

children.name: Sunni
children.summary: The largest Islamic tradition; includes Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali legal schools among other currents.

children.name: Hanafi
children.summary: Sunni legal school widespread across South and Central Asia, Turkey and the Balkans.

children.name: Maliki
children.summary: Sunni legal school prominent in North and West Africa.

children.name: Shafi'i
children.summary: Sunni legal school prominent in East Africa and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Hanbali
children.summary: Sunni legal school with strong historical presence in the Arabian Peninsula.

children.name: Shia
children.summary: Major Islamic tradition including Twelver, Ismaili and Zaydi communities.

children.name: Twelver
children.summary: Largest Shia branch.

children.name: Ismaili
children.summary: Shia branch with several living communities.

children.name: Zaydi
children.summary: Shia branch historically centered in Yemen.

children.name: Ibadi
children.summary: Distinct early Islamic tradition, especially associated with Oman.

children.name: Religiously unaffiliated
children.summary: People who identify with no religion, including atheists, agnostics and people who say they have no particular religion.

children.name: Atheist
children.summary: No belief in gods; not a single philosophical system.

children.name: Agnostic
children.summary: Religious or metaphysical knowledge is uncertain or not claimed.

children.name: Nothing in particular
children.summary: No formal religious identity; beliefs and practices vary widely.

children.name: Hinduism
children.summary: A large family of traditions centered mainly in South Asia rather than one centralized church.

children.name: Vaishnavism
children.summary: Vishnu- and avatar-centered Hindu traditions.

children.name: Shaivism
children.summary: Shiva-centered Hindu traditions.

children.name: Shaktism
children.summary: Goddess-centered Hindu traditions.

children.name: Smartism
children.summary: Smarta tradition emphasizing multiple forms of the divine and Advaita-influenced practice.

children.name: Buddhism
children.summary: Pew estimated 324 million Buddhists globally in 2020.

children.name: Mahayana
children.summary: Large family of East Asian Buddhist traditions, including Chan/Zen and Pure Land.

children.name: Theravada
children.summary: Pali-canon tradition prominent in Sri Lanka and mainland Southeast Asia.

children.name: Vajrayana
children.summary: Tantric Buddhist traditions especially associated with Tibet and the Himalayan region.

children.name: Other religions
children.summary: Pew's combined category includes many distinct religions. It should not be read as one tradition.

children.name: Sikhism
children.summary: Monotheistic tradition founded in Punjab around the teachings of the Sikh Gurus.

children.name: Bahá'í
children.summary: Global monotheistic religion founded in the nineteenth century.

children.name: Jainism
children.summary: Indian religious tradition emphasizing nonviolence, discipline and liberation.

children.name: Daoist / Chinese religious traditions
children.summary: Daoist, folk, ancestral and other Chinese religious practices overlap in ways that resist a simple denomination tree.

children.name: Shinto
children.summary: Japanese tradition centered on kami, ritual, place and community.

children.name: Folk / traditional religions
children.summary: Many local and indigenous traditions that should not be collapsed into one theology.

children.name: Judaism
children.summary: Pew estimated 14.8 million Jews worldwide in 2020.

children.name: Orthodox
children.summary: Jewish movements treating halakhah as binding, with Modern Orthodox and Haredi communities among them.

children.name: Conservative / Masorti
children.summary: Modern Jewish movement balancing tradition and historical development.

children.name: Reform / Progressive
children.summary: Jewish movements emphasizing ethical monotheism, adaptation and individual/community autonomy.

children.name: Secular / cultural Jewish identity
children.summary: Jewish peoplehood and culture without necessarily religious observance.
